HTML pages inside DeepSeekRuntime conversations — previews, reports, and forms that can answer back.
# dsh-surface
**Live pages in the conversation. Preview, report, or ask.**
`dsh-surface` is a DeepSeekRuntime plugin that renders a complete HTML page inside the conversation.
Use it for UI previews, data reports, mockups, calculators — or for forms and approvals where the p
age can send a structured answer back to the agent **through the same tool call**.
## Why
Most chat UIs can show text or a fixed component tree. A page is different: it can lay out a real re
port, run a chart, look exactly like the UI you are building, and collect an answer without making t
he user translate their choice into prose.
`dsh-surface` gives the model one tool:
- **render a page** — a self-contained HTML document, sandboxed, themed with the host's tokens, auto

-sized;
- **optionally wait for it** — the tool call blocks until the user submits, cancels, or the

timeout expires;
- **return data, not prose** — the page calls `dshSurface.submit(data, summary)` an
d the agent receives `{ answered, summary, data }` in the same turn.
It is not a component library, and it is not an artifact manager. It is the page surface between the
model and the user.
## Features

- **Any self-contained HTML** — inline CSS/JS, SVG, canvas; no external requests.
- **Sandboxed by d
efault** — opaque origin, no `allow-same-origin`, CSP blocks network, forms, nested frames, and top-

level navigation.
- **Follows the host theme** — `--dsw-*` tokens are bridged to `--background`, `--

foreground`, `--chart-*`, `--radius`, and friends.
- **Auto height** — the frame reports its content

height and the card sizes itself.
- **Blocking answers** — `awaitAnswer`-style semantics without a

separate question panel.
- **OpenChamber-compatible pages** — `window.openchamber.submit(data, summa

ry)` is an alias of `window.dshSurface`.
- **Small and auditable** — one host file, one client bundl
e, a 12-case test suite.
## Install
Requires DeepSeekRuntime with the Web UI (`dsh web`) and Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24`.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Restart `dsh web`, then refresh the browser. The plugin activates on the next session.
> The package is published as `dsh-surface`. If you are installing from a checkout instead, use `dsh
plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-surface` and run `npm install && npm run build` first.
## Use it
Ask for a page, or point the model at one:
> Render a one-page Q3 revenue report with a bar chart and a table. Use the `render` tool; make the
page self-contained.
> Here is our release checklist. Render it as a page with an approve / reject choice and a note fiel
d. On submit call `dshSurface.submit({ decision, note }, summary)`.
The model calls the `render` tool with a complete HTML document. The page appears in the tool card.
If it calls `dshSurface.submit`, the call stays open until the answer arrives.

## Security model
- The page runs in an iframe with `sandbox="allow-scripts allow-forms"` and **no** `allow-same-origi

n`. It has an opaque origin and cannot read the host page, cookies, or storage.
- A document-level C
SP allows inline scripts/styles and `data:` images, and blocks `connect-src`, nested frames, forms,

and navigation.
- The submission route is registered on the host's authenticated `/api` channel (`ct
x.connection.fetch`). Only the owner peer reaches it; the host checks Host/Origin and browser authen

tication before the handler runs.
- Payload limits: 500-character summary, 16 KB JSON data, 200 KB H

TML.
- Pages should not ask for secrets. Treat any page content as untrusted.
See docs/architecture.md for the full lifecycle.
## Compatibility
| Surface                | Status
e                | Status                                                                          |
| `dsh web` (0.2.1-rc.2) | Tested end to end

|
| dsh headless / TUI     | No page surface; the tool waits until its timeout and returns `a

nswered: false` |
| Desktop (Electron)     | Not yet verified; custom `fetch` over the desktop IPC b
ridge needs a real run   |
## Known limitations
1. **The page folds when the turn ends.** The card lives inside the tool-call group; after the turn
settles, that group collapses. The answer remains visible in the transcript, and expanding the group

brings the page back. A `conversation.chat.turnTail` card is the planned fix.
2. **No local images
yet.** Only `data:` / inline images render; reading workspace files and enforcing a budget is not im

plemented.
3. **HTML lives in the tool arguments.** A large page is part of the session log and may

be resent with later turns. An artifact-backed page (short id + file) is the planned improvement.
4.
**No waiting notification.** If you switch sessions, nothing tells you that a page is waiting; the

tool does not appear in a global inbox.
5. **A host restart loses the wait.** The pending map is in

memory; after a restart the call is interrupted and the page becomes read-only.
6. **No persistence
or versions.** The plugin stores nothing of its own; every render is a new call.
